RRO is an enhanced distribution of R. RRO 3.2.2 includes R 3.2.2,  and is therefore fully compatibility with all packages, scripts and applications that work with that version of R.

Cheers,
Josee Martens

Look for the clause that starts with:

sysinfo((["sysname"]=="Darwin"

Comment out the message line that follows the Darwin sysinfo line.

Josée

The checkpoint package <https://mran.microsoft.com/documents/rro/reproducibility/#timemachine> included with Microsoft R Open likewise uses HTTPS when downloading R package versions for reproducible data analysis.

If you're new to Microsoft R Open, here are some tips to get started, <https://mran.microsoft.com/documents/getting-started/> and there are many data sources you can explore with MRO <https://mran.microsoft.com/documents/data/>. Thanks go as always to the contributors to the R Project <https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/what-is-r/#contributors> upon which RRO is built.

I had the exact same problem installing MKL on Windows 10 64-bit with pre/co-existing R3.2.3 | Rstudio latest.

Solved it by locating the msi file that was extracted during the install - it was in my temp directory - called "tmpB5D2.tmp.msi" but I think this name varies - and just executed the install process directly using that msi file. It appears to work as confirmed by "
Multithreaded BLAS/LAPACK libraries detected. Using 4 cores for math algorithms."

and appears as RevoMath-3.2.3 under Programs | Uninstall

Unhandled exception at 0x000007FEFEB87D0F (msvcrt.dll) in Rgui.exe: 0xC0000005: Access violation reading location 0x0000000000000000.

- Type commands or characters until they reach the right edge of the RGui window

- MRO will crash and report the above error upon launching debugger

Crashes begin after the window is made larger by at least 10%, or full screen, or full height, or similar measures in between.  Horizontal resizing of the window has no effect.  /Shrinking/ the vertical size of the window to smaller than default size has no effect.

- Enabling "Prevent windows from being automatically arranged..." in control panel has no effect

Hi Jake,

If I understand correctly, you are trying to install the MKL after installing Micorosoft R Open to a non-default folder.
Unfortunately, I don't think we support that kind of configuration directly at the moment, though we certainly should.

You can work around the issue however by manually installing the MKL files to the proper location as follows:

1).  Cd to the directory '$RHOME/lib64/R/lib on your system( by default this is '/usr/lib64/MRO-3.2.3/R-3.2.3/lib64/R/lib')
2).  Rename the files 'libRlapack.so' and 'libRblas.so' to 'libRlapack.so.keep' and 'libRblas.so.keep'.
3).  Change directory to the directory where you installed the 'RevoMath' folder.
4).  Copy all of the files in this folder to the '$RHOME/lib64/R/lib' folder.
5).  Install the 'RevoUtilsMath' package as follows:   'R CMD INSTALL RevoUtilsMath.tar.gz'

This manual install should work - let me know if you have any problems with it.

Stephen Weller
Microsoft R Open Technical Support

Some RStudio users who have recently downloaded MRO 3.2.3 may encounter an error when they try to create a new R Markdown file from the RStudio IDE. The error informs the user that the available rmarkdown package is not the version required by RStudio. It appears that the rmarkdown package was updated on 1/1/2016 just after the CRAN snapshot was taken that day. Since MRO 3.2.3 uses the 1/1/2016 static CRAN snapshot by default, the fix is as easy as pointing to a more recent version of the package or a more recent repository.

Here’s how. Use ONE of the following solutions:

Get the latest version of the `rmarkdown` package using
install.packages("rmarkdown", repos = "https://cran.revolutionanalytics.com")

Get the 0.9.2 version of the `rmarkdown` package using:
install.packages("rmarkdown", repos = "https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/snapshot/2016-01-02")
Use the R `options()` function:
options(repos = "https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/snapshot/2016-01-02")

By default, Microsoft R Open offers its users predictability using a static CRAN snapshot date. For example, the CRAN repository for MRO 3.2.3 is configured to point to a snapshot date of Jan 1, 2016. Consequently, with MRO 3.2.3 you'll always get packages as they were at midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2016 by default whenever you use  install.packages. However, as demonstrated above, it is still possible to get packages, such as rmarkdown from another date.
